newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end flat in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end flat in active trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed mixed with a negative bias on Thursday in brisk trading powered by activity in bank stocks, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares slipped 0.09 percent, or 0.24 points, to 274.39 on heavy all-share turnover of 207 million shekels against 215 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.15 percent lower at 282.78.
Traders said the session opened with mild gains but profit taking towards the end of the day reversed the trend, with most of the activity concentrated in bank shares.

"Last week was a landmark for the Tel Aviv stock market. Activity rose and the indices reached new highs. The market gained momentum and now it is clear that the market can also absorb a huge offering without showing weakness," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.
"This is only the beginning of a new rally. We might see a technical correction next week but the positive trend is clear," Nahum said.

A public offering for 15 percent of the share capital of Bank Leumi, Israel's second largest bank, closed at 12 percent above the minimum price on Tuesday. The offering, the biggest ever on the Tel Aviv market, was 2.8 times oversubscribed.
Bank Leumi, the most active share on Thursday, fell 0.75 percent to 526 agorot on volume of 29.6 million shekels.
Ron Weisberg at I.B.I Investment House described the market as very strong.
"The strength of the market is surprising and the recent rise was led by local investors. We see that more investors move money from unlinked bonds to stocks," he said.
Weisberg added that the recent recovery of the primary market and heavier volume indicated the market would continue to rise.
"We might see a mild correction but in the near term the positive trend will gain momentum," he said.

Bank Hapoalim, the second most active issue, rose 2.75 percent to 768 agorot. The bank reported on Thursday that net profit rose 46 percent in the first quarter of 1997 to 316 million shekels from 216 million a year earlier.
IDB Development Corp fell 2.0 percent to 8,414 agorot. The company said on Thursday earnings per share in the first quarter of 1997 fell to 1.40 shekels from 1.46 a year earlier.

IDB's parent company, IDB Holdings Corp, dropped 1.0 percent to 7,750 agorot. The company reported on Thursday that earnings per share rose in the first quarter to 1.21 shekels from 1.15 shekels in the same period last year.
Blue Square Chain Stores plunged 7.5 percent to 3,476 agorot. The company said net profit fell in the first quarter to six million shekels from 14.7 million shekels.
Africa Israel Investments rose 2.0 percent to 24,710 agorot. Africa said on Thursday net profit in the first quarter fell to 14.1 million shekels from 37 million shekels in the same period in 1996.
Mofet Israel Technology Fund rose 0.5 percent to 192 agorot. Mofet reported earnings per share climbed to 14 agorot from eight agorot a year earlier.
Bezeq Israel Telcom, the third most active share, fell 2.0 percent to 911 on volume of 9.3 million shekels.
($1 = 3.39 shekels)
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
